title: Recognizing the Binding Pattern and Dissociation Pathways of the p300 Taz2-p53 TAD2 Complex.
authors: Li, Tongtong; Motta, Stefano; Stevens, Amy O; Song, Shenghan; Hendrix, Emily; Pandini, Alessandro; He, Yi
one_liner_zh: 该文用MD、SMD、自组织映射和TRFDA研究p53 TAD2与p300 Taz2复合物的解离路径与关键残基，聚焦转录因子无序区与共激活因子蛋白-DNA相关互作机制，方法高度契合本课题。
abstract: The dynamic association and dissociation between proteins are the basis of cellular signal transduction. This process becomes much more complicated if one or both interaction partners are intrinsically disordered because intrinsically disordered proteins can undergo disorder-to-order transitions upon binding to their partners. p53, a transcription factor with disordered regions, plays significant roles in many cellular signaling pathways. It is critical to understand the binding/unbinding mechanism involving these disordered regions of p53 at the residue level to reveal how p53 performs its biological functions. Here, we studied the dissociation process of the intrinsically disordered N-terminal transactivation domain 2 (TAD2) of p53 and the transcriptional adaptor zinc-binding 2 (Taz2) domain of transcriptional coactivator p300 using a combination of classical molecular dynamics, steered molecular dynamics, self-organizing maps, and time-resolved force distribution analysis (TRFDA). We observed two different dissociation pathways with different probabilities. One dissociation pathway starts from the TAD2 N-terminus and propagates to the alpha-helix and finally the C-terminus. The other dissociation pathway is in the opposite order. Subsequent TRFDA results reveal that key residues in TAD2 play critical roles. Besides the residues in agreement with previous experimental results, we also highlighted some other residues that play important roles in the disassociation process. In the dissociation process, non-native interactions were formed to partially compensate for the energy loss due to the breaking of surrounding native interactions. Moreover, our statistical analysis results of other experimentally determined complex structures involving either Taz2 or TAD2 suggest that the binding of the Taz2-TAD2 complex is mainly governed by the binding site of Taz2, which includes three main binding regions. Therefore, the complexes involving Taz2 may follow similar binding/unbinding behaviors, which could be studied together to generate common principles.
abstract_zh: 蛋白质之间的动态结合与解离是细胞信号转导的基础。当相互作用伙伴中一方或双方为固有无序蛋白时，这一过程变得更加复杂，因为固有无序蛋白在与伙伴结合时可发生从无序到有序的转变。p53是一种含有无序区域的转录因子，在许多细胞信号通路中发挥重要作用。在残基水平上理解涉及p53这些无序区域的结合/解离机制，对于揭示p53如何执行其生物学功能至关重要。在此，我们结合经典分子动力学 (molecular dynamics)、拉伸分子动力学 (steered molecular dynamics)、自组织映射 (self-organizing maps) 和时间分辨力分布分析 (time-resolved force distribution analysis, TRFDA)，研究了p53的固有无序N端反式激活结构域2 (transactivation domain 2, TAD2) 与转录共激活因子p300的转录适配器锌结合2 (zinc-binding 2, Taz2) 结构域的解离过程。我们观察到两种具有不同概率的解离路径。一种解离路径从TAD2的N端开始，传播至α-螺旋，最后到达C端。另一种解离路径则顺序相反。随后的TRFDA结果表明，TAD2中的关键残基发挥重要作用。除了与先前实验结果一致的残基外，我们还强调了其他在解离过程中发挥重要作用的残基。在解离过程中，形成了非天然相互作用，以部分补偿因周围天然相互作用断裂而导致的能量损失。此外，我们对其他实验确定的涉及Taz2或TAD2的复合物结构的统计分析结果表明，Taz2-TAD2复合物的结合主要由Taz2的结合位点控制，该位点包含三个主要结合区域。因此，涉及Taz2的复合物可能遵循类似的结合/解离行为，可共同研究以生成通用原则。
